title: The Day of the First Planting
skyStory: Still in Capricorn at eighty-four percent, the moon has rolled up its sleeves and joined the great long weekend planting. Half of Atlantic Canada is on its knees in the garden, and the other half is warning them about frost. The moon sides with the planters. Saturn, ruler of the goat, quietly checks the forecast anyway. Mars has already planted something upside down.

reading: Your hands want to be in the dirt today, and the Capricorn moon agrees. Plant something, anything: a single tomato seedling, a pot of herbs, a sunflower seed pushed into the soil with your thumb. The Fire Tiger digging is a sight to behold, and also slightly chaotic.

Here's the deal with seeds. You can't make them grow faster by watching. The [[Seven of Pentacles]] reminds you that good things take a whole season. So plant, water, and walk away. Tonight, sit by the cabin with dirt under your nails and a sense of having done exactly enough. That feeling is rarer than it should be. Notice it.
joel.mission: Plant one seed, seedling or bulb today, and give it a name worthy of a fantasy novel hero.
joel.omen: An earthworm surfacing right where you're digging. You're in the right spot; keep going.
joel.stoneWhy: a seed of light in dark soil

reading: Another day of moon in your sign, and you're on a roll. People come to you with questions, and you somehow have every answer. It's not magic. It's years of noticing. The Wood Rat has been taking notes since before anyone else woke up.

Take a minute before lunch to watch your hands while you talk. Watch them dance. Five stones, five elements, every one catching light: onyx for earth, ruby for fire, mother of pearl for water, diamonds for wind, and the ruby again for heart. Together they summon something no single ring could. The [[Queen of Wands]] approves of every sparkle.
nancy.mission: Tell one story today and deliberately count how many different gestures your hands make while you tell it.
nancy.omen: A rainbow caught in a garden sprinkler. All five elements are lining up for you today.
nancy.elementWhy: the fifth element ties it all

together.text: Plant something today, both of you, then send the other a photo of the spot where it's buried. No seedlings visible, just dirt. Agree to check back in three weeks with progress photos. Whoever sprouts first gets to name the other's plant.

game.intro: Planting day. Ten seconds a pair, which Saturn insists is how long a seed takes to sprout.
